Each link goes to the project's own site. A line with a plus sign opens a list.

## For Your Research

<details class="pv-fold">
<summary>Datasets</summary>

[Global Populism Database](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/LFTQEZ)
: How populist the speeches of presidents and prime ministers are, across countries and terms of office, coded by hand. Hosted on Harvard Dataverse.

[The PopuList](https://popu-list.org)
: Populist, far-left and far-right parties in Europe since 1989, classified with the help of country experts.

[V-Party](https://www.v-dem.net/data/v-party-dataset/)
: The V-Dem Institute's dataset on the policy positions and organisation of political parties across the world.

[Chapel Hill Expert Survey (CHES)](https://www.chesdata.eu)
: Expert estimates of where national parties in Europe stand on European integration, ideology and policy issues, in waves since 1999.

[Populism and Political Parties Expert Survey (POPPA)](https://poppa-data.eu/)
: Expert ratings of how populist the parties of Europe are: 312 parties in 31 countries in 2023, after a first round in 2018.

[Global Party Survey](https://doi.org/10.1177/1354068820927686)
: An expert survey of parties around the world that also rates how populist their rhetoric is. The link goes to the article that presents it (Norris 2020).

</details>

<details class="pv-fold">
<summary>Other Hubs</summary>

[European Center for Populism Studies (ECPS)](https://www.populismstudies.org)
: An independent centre in Brussels for research on and analysis of populism.

[Illiberalism Studies Hub](https://hub.illiberalism.org/)
: A database of academic articles on illiberalism, kept by the Illiberalism Studies Program at George Washington University.

[Team Populism](https://populism.byu.edu)
: A network of scholars who study the causes and consequences of populism. Its site hosts datasets and papers.

[POPULISMUS](https://populismus.gr)
: An observatory of populist discourse at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki.

</details>

<details class="pv-fold">
<summary>Tools for Measuring Populism in Text</summary>

Six ways to measure populism in speeches, manifestos and posts, each in the article that presents it.

- Hawkins 2009. [Is Chávez Populist?: Measuring Populist Discourse in Comparative Perspective](https://doi.org/10.1177/0010414009331721). *Comparative Political Studies*. Speeches graded as a whole by trained readers.
- Rooduijn and Pauwels 2011. [Measuring Populism: Comparing Two Methods of Content Analysis](https://doi.org/10.1080/01402382.2011.616665). *West European Politics*. A dictionary of words, tested against coding by hand.
- Aslanidis 2018. [Measuring populist discourse with semantic text analysis: an application on grassroots populist mobilization](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11135-017-0517-4). *Quality & Quantity*. Semantic text analysis.
- Gründl 2022. [Populist ideas on social media: A dictionary-based measurement of populist communication](https://doi.org/10.1177/1461444820976970). *New Media & Society*. A dictionary for posts on social media.
- Di Cocco and Monechi 2022. [How Populist are Parties? Measuring Degrees of Populism in Party Manifestos Using Supervised Machine Learning](https://doi.org/10.1017/pan.2021.29). *Political Analysis*. Supervised machine learning on party manifestos.
- Bonikowski et al. 2022. [Politics as Usual? Measuring Populism, Nationalism, and Authoritarianism in U.S. Presidential Campaigns (1952–2020) with Neural Language Models](https://doi.org/10.1177/00491241221122317). *Sociological Methods & Research*. Neural language models on campaign speeches.

[Every work on measurement in the Library](../library/index.html?approach=measurement)

</details>

<details class="pv-fold">
<summary>Networks and Groups</summary>

[ECPR Standing Group on Extremism & Democracy](https://ecpr.eu/group/extremism-democracy)
: The group of the European Consortium for Political Research for scholars of extremism, radicalism and populism, founded in 1999. Its newsletter is e-Extreme.

[PSA Populism Specialist Group](https://psapopulism.org/)
: The group of the Political Studies Association for the study of populist discourses, movements and parties. It runs a workshop every year and a podcast, and was the association's specialist group of the year in 2025.

[IDEoPOP Doctoral Network](https://ideopop.populism-internationalrelations.com/)
: A network of seven universities, funded by the European Union, training doctoral researchers on how populism shapes international politics. The universities are Freiburg, Sciences Po Paris, Gothenburg, Bilkent, Genoa, Jagiellonian and Bath.

[Center for Research on Extremism (C-REX)](https://www.sv.uio.no/c-rex/english/)
: A centre at the University of Oslo, and a network of researchers across countries, on the far right, hate crime and political violence.

</details>

<details class="pv-fold">
<summary>Method Schools in the Social Sciences</summary>

Where to learn the methods behind this kind of research. Each school takes researchers from any country, and most teach online as well as in person.

[ECPR Methods School](https://ecpr.eu/methodsschool)
: Qualitative and quantitative training from the European Consortium for Political Research, as a summer school at a European university and a winter school online.

[MethodsNET Summer School](https://methodsnet.org)
: Three weeks of social research methods every summer, held with the Central European University in Vienna.

[Konstanz Methods Excellence Workshops (KOMEX)](https://afww.uni-konstanz.de/en/komex/konstanz-methods-excellence-workshops)
: Short and longer courses every February at the University of Konstanz, with MethodsNET, in person and online, with fellowships for some applicants.

[Summer School in Social Sciences Methods](https://www.ssm.usi.ch/en)
: Two weeks each August at the Università della Svizzera italiana in Lugano, with FORS, the Swiss centre for social science research. It has run for thirty years.

[ICPSR Summer Program](https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/web/pages/sumprog/)
: Statistics and quantitative methods at the University of Michigan, running since 1963, in person and online.

</details>

## For Your Career

<details class="pv-fold">
<summary>Jobs and Fellowships</summary>

[EURAXESS](https://euraxess.ec.europa.eu/jobs)
: The European Commission's portal of research jobs, funding and fellowships across Europe. Hosts that support applications for MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships advertise there too.

[jobs.ac.uk](https://www.jobs.ac.uk)
: The largest board of academic posts in the United Kingdom, which also carries jobs elsewhere in Europe and beyond, from doctoral studentships to professorships.

[Academic Positions](https://academicpositions.com)
: Doctoral, postdoctoral and faculty posts across Europe. Free to search, with alerts by email.

</details>

<details class="pv-fold">
<summary>Grants</summary>

[MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships](https://marie-sklodowska-curie-actions.ec.europa.eu/)
: Fellowships of the European Union for researchers who hold a PhD, of any nationality. European Fellowships last 12 to 24 months.

[MSCA Doctoral Networks](https://marie-sklodowska-curie-actions.ec.europa.eu/)
: Funded PhD positions in networks of universities. The positions are advertised on EURAXESS.

[European Research Council (ERC)](https://erc.europa.eu)
: Starting, Consolidator, Advanced and Synergy Grants for researchers who lead their own project.

</details>
